title: Return intended status codes through the edge
statement: The status code a reader or crawler receives is the one the origin produced, and the edge does not substitute its own success, error, or challenge status for it.
rationale: When the edge rewrites the status, the origin's answer about whether a page exists never reaches the requester, so a missing page can be reported as present and a working page as unavailable.
implementation: Compare the status for each response class at the edge against the same request made directly to the origin, and correct the edge rule rather than adjusting the origin to compensate. Custom error pages must be served with the original code, not with a success code.

verification.method: Request representative existing, missing, redirecting, and failing routes through the edge and directly against the origin, and compare the status codes.

sources.title: How HTTP status codes, and network and DNS errors, affect Google Search

title: Allow verified search crawlers to reach public pages
statement: Requests from crawlers the site intends to permit are served the same public pages a reader receives, and any bot-management rule that would block them is scoped to exclude them after verification by the documented method.
rationale: A blocked crawler cannot distinguish being blocked from the page not existing, and the block is invisible from inside the site because every human request succeeds.
implementation: Verify crawler identity by reverse and forward DNS lookup or by the published address ranges, not by the user-agent string alone, and express the exemption in terms of that verification. Do not widen a rule to any client claiming the user agent.

verification.method: Request public pages with each declared crawler user agent from an address the site treats as unverified and from one it verifies, and record both outcomes.

caution: Permitting a crawler to fetch a page does not cause the page to be indexed. This control removes an obstacle rather than producing an outcome.

sources.title: Verifying Googlebot and other Google crawlers

title: Serve public pages without an interactive challenge
statement: Pages the site wants discovered do not require solving a challenge, executing a proof-of-work interstitial, or holding a prior session cookie before the content is delivered.
rationale: A challenge served in place of the page returns an error status or a page whose only content is the challenge, so the content behind it is absent from whatever the requester received.
implementation: Restrict challenges to routes that accept input or cost money to serve, and leave content routes unchallenged. Where load requires protection, rate limiting by address preserves access for a compliant crawler in a way a challenge does not.

verification.method: Request public content routes from an unrecognised network with no cookies and confirm the response body is the page rather than a challenge document.

title: Keep protocol files reachable through the edge
statement: The crawl directive file, the sitemap, and any ownership verification file the site publishes are served from the paths the relevant specification or platform requires, with no rule at the edge rewriting, blocking, or redirecting them elsewhere.
rationale: Each of these files is fetched from a fixed location, so a rule that catches the path pattern removes the whole mechanism rather than degrading it, and nothing on the site indicates the loss.
implementation: Add explicit pass-through rules for these paths ahead of any broad blocking or redirecting rule, and test them per host rather than only on the primary hostname.

verification.method: Request each protocol path on every public host through the edge and record the status, content type, and any redirect applied.

title: Resolve redirects consistently at the edge and the origin
statement: A given request produces the same final URL whether the redirect rule lives at the edge or in the application, and the two layers do not each apply their own version of the same rule.
rationale: Two layers rewriting the same request produce a chain where one hop was intended, and the duplication is invisible unless the full chain is recorded rather than only the final result.
implementation: Choose one layer to own each class of rewrite, document which owns what, and remove the duplicate from the other. Host and scheme normalisation usually belongs at the edge, while route-level moves belong in the application.

verification.method: Record the complete redirect chain for a set of known aliases through the edge, then repeat directly against the origin and compare hop counts and final URLs.

title: Preserve indexing headers through the edge
statement: Response headers that carry indexing meaning - the robots tag, the canonical link, the content language, the content type - arrive at the requester unaltered by the edge, and the edge does not add its own copies of them.
rationale: A stripped header removes an instruction the origin issued, and an added one issues an instruction the origin never made, in both cases changing how the page is treated without any change to the application.
implementation: Compare the header set at the edge against the origin for each response class and remove any transform that drops or injects these headers. Where the edge must add a header, add it in one place and record why.

verification.method: Diff the full response header set between the edge and the origin for one URL per response class.
